claims: The 25th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution was ratified in 1967.
The 25th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution was ratified following President John F. Kennedy's assassination.
Section 1 of the 25th Amendment explicitly states that if the President is removed, dies, or resigns, the Vice President becomes President.
Section 2 of the 25th Amendment allows the President to nominate a new Vice President if the office becomes vacant.
A nomination under Section 2 of the 25th Amendment is subject to confirmation by a majority vote of both houses of Congress.
Under Section 3 of the 25th Amendment, the President may declare in writing they are unable to perform duties.
A declaration under Section 3 makes the Vice President the Acting President until a written declaration to the contrary is submitted.
Section 4 of the 25th Amendment authorizes the Vice President and a majority of the Cabinet (or another body authorized by Congress) to declare the President unable to perform their duties.
A declaration under Section 4 makes the Vice President the Acting President.
If the President disputes the incapacity under Section 4, Congress must decide the issue within 48 hours.
A two-thirds vote in both houses is required to keep the Vice President in power under Section 4.
Section 4 of the 25th Amendment has never been formally invoked.
Section 2 of the 25th Amendment was used to appoint Gerald Ford in 1973 after Spiro Agnew resigned.
Section 2 of the 25th Amendment was used to appoint Nelson Rockefeller in 1974 after Ford became President.
Section 3 of the 25th Amendment was used by President Reagan in 1985 before surgery.
Section 3 of the 25th Amendment was used by President George W. Bush in 2002 for medical procedures.
Section 3 of the 25th Amendment was used by President George W. Bush in 2007 for medical procedures
